sentences.zh: 皇帝冕服 后妃冠服 皇太子親王以下冠服

translations.literal: Emperor's Court Robes and Crown; Empress and Consorts' Crowns and Robes; Crown Prince, Princes, and Those Below — Crowns and Robes
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sacrificial robes and crowns; crowns and dress for empresses and consorts; crowns and dress for the crown prince, princes, and those of lower rank

sentences.zh: 皇帝冕服：洪武元年，學士陶安請制五冕。

translations.literal: The emperor's court robes and crown: In the first year of Hongwu, Academician Tao An requested the establishment of the five caps.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's sacrificial dress: In Hongwu 1 (1368), Academician Tao An petitioned to institute the five ceremonial caps.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「此禮太繁。

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "This ritual is too cumbersome.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu said, "This ceremony is overly elaborate.

sentences.zh: 祭天地、宗廟，服袞冕。

translations.literal: When sacrificing to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples, wear the sacrificial crown and robe.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples, wear the full ceremonial crown and robe.

sentences.zh: 社稷等祀，服通天冠，絳紗袍。

translations.literal: For sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain and the like, wear the Communication-with-Heaven Cap and deep-red gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: For rites at the altars of soil and grain and comparable ceremonies, wear the Communication-with-Heaven Cap and a deep-red gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 餘不用。

translations.literal: The rest are not to be used.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder are not to be used.

sentences.zh: 」三年，更定正旦、冬至、聖節並服袞冕，祭社稷、先農、冊拜，亦如之。

translations.literal: " In the third year, it was revised that New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and imperial birthday all required the sacrificial crown and robe; sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain, the God of Agriculture, and investiture audiences were treated the same.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third year the rule was fixed: New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and the emperor's birthday all required the full ceremonial crown and robe, and sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain, the God of Agriculture, and formal investiture audiences followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 十六年，定袞冕之制。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the regulations for the sacrificial crown and robe were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the system for the ceremonial crown and robe was established.

sentences.zh: 冕，前圓後方，玄表纁裡。

translations.literal: The crown: round in front and square behind, dark on the outside and deep red within.
translations.idiomatic: The crown was round in front and square behind, with a dark outer surface and deep-red lining.

sentences.zh: 前後各十二旒，旒五采，玉十二，珠五，採繅十有二就，就相去一寸。

translations.literal: Front and rear each had twelve pendants; the pendants were five-colored; jade twelve; beads five; colored silks with twelve tassels, the tassels one inch apart.
translations.idiomatic: There were twelve pendants before and behind; the pendants were in five colors, with twelve jade pieces, five beads, and twelve colored silk tassels spaced one inch apart.

sentences.zh: 紅絲組為纓，黈纊充耳，玉簪導。

translations.literal: Red silk cords served as the chin strap; yellow silk plugs filled the ears; a jade hairpin guided it.
translations.idiomatic: Red silk cords formed the chin strap, yellow silk plugs filled the ears, and a jade hairpin secured the crown.

sentences.zh: 袞，玄衣黃裳，十二章，日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲六章織於衣，宗彝、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻六章繡於裳。

translations.literal: The sacrificial robe: dark upper garment and yellow lower garment, twelve emblems — sun, moon, stars, mountain, dragon, and flowering creature, six emblems woven on the robe; ritual vessels, waterweed, fire, millet grain, axe-and-gouge, and opposed triangles, six emblems embroidered on the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial robe had a dark upper garment and yellow skirt with twelve emblems: sun, moon, stars, mountain, dragon, and flowering creature were woven on the robe; ritual vessels, waterweed, fire, millet grain, axe-and-gouge, and opposed triangles were embroidered on the skirt.

sentences.zh: 白羅大帶，紅裡。

translations.literal: A great belt of white gauze, red lining.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt was white gauze with a red lining.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝隨裳色，繡龍、火、山文。

translations.literal: The knee cover followed the skirt's color, embroidered with dragon, fire, and mountain designs.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover matched the skirt in color and was embroidered with dragon, fire, and mountain motifs.

sentences.zh: 玉革帶，玉佩。

translations.literal: A jade-studded leather belt and jade pendants.
translations.idiomatic: There was a leather belt set with jade and jade pendants.

translations.literal: The great sash had six colors — red, yellow, black, white, pale crimson, and green; three small sashes, the colors the same as the great sash.
translations.idiomatic: The great ceremonial sash used six colors—red, yellow, black, white, pale crimson, and green—with three smaller sashes in matching colors.

sentences.zh: 間施三玉環。

translations.literal: Three jade rings were set between them.
translations.idiomatic: Three jade rings were spaced along them.

translations.literal: An inner robe of white gauze, collar with opposed-triangle pattern, green edging on the cuffs.
translations.idiomatic: The inner robe was white gauze with an opposed-triangle collar and green trim on the cuffs.

sentences.zh: 黃襪黃舄，金飾。

translations.literal: Yellow stockings and yellow court shoes, with gold ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow stockings and yellow court shoes were ornamented with gold.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，更定袞冕十二章。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, the sacrificial crown and robe with twelve emblems were revised.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the twelve-emblem ceremonial crown and robe were revised again.

sentences.zh: 冕版廣一尺二寸，長二尺四寸。

translations.literal: The crown board was one foot two inches wide and two feet four inches long.
translations.idiomatic: The crown board measured one foot two inches in width and two feet four in length.

sentences.zh: 冠上有復，玄表朱裡，餘如舊制。

translations.literal: Above the cap was a covering, dark outside and vermilion within; the rest followed the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: A covering was placed above the cap, dark on the outside and vermilion within; everything else followed the earlier regulations.

translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial robe had a dark upper garment and deep-red skirt with twelve emblems, as in the earlier regulations.

sentences.zh: 中單以素紗為之。

translations.literal: The inner robe was made of plain gauze.
translations.idiomatic: The inner robe was made of plain gauze.

translations.literal: A knee cover of red gauze, one foot wide above, two feet wide below, three feet long, woven with fire, dragon, and mountain, three emblems.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover was red gauze, one foot wide at the top, two at the bottom, and three feet long, woven with the fire, dragon, and mountain emblems.

sentences.zh: 革帶佩玉，長三尺三寸。

translations.literal: A leather belt with jade pendants, three feet three inches long.
translations.idiomatic: The leather belt bore jade pendants and was three feet three inches long.

sentences.zh: 大帶素表朱裡，兩邊用緣，上以朱錦，下以綠錦。

translations.idiomatic: The great belt was plain on the outside and vermilion within, with edging on both sides; vermilion brocade above and green brocade below.

translations.literal: Fixed in the third year of Yongle: the ceremonial crown was made of black gauze; the upper covering was called the tassel-band; paulownia board served as the core, clothed in fine silk, dark outside and vermilion within, round in front and square behind.

translations.literal: and the places where the chin strap was attached were all ornamented with gold.

translations.idiomatic: The jade tablet was one foot two inches long, its upper end tapered and carved with four mountains to represent the mountains of the four quarters—essentially the Zhou quarter-tablet, unlike the great tablet, which was left uncarved.

translations.literal: Yellow brocade bound its lower part; separately a pouch sheathed it, with golden dragon designs.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow brocade bound its lower end, and a separate pouch sheathed it, ornamented with golden dragons.

translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial robe bore twelve emblems.

translations.literal: The dark upper garment had eight emblems: sun, moon, and dragon on the shoulders; stars and mountain on the back; fire, flowering creature, and ritual vessels on the sleeves,

translations.literal: The deep-red skirt had four emblems, woven with waterweed, millet grain, axe-and-gouge, and opposed triangles, two each; three panels in front, four behind; front and rear not joined, sharing the waist; with a pleated fold; proper-color edging on the sides and hem.

sentences.zh: 裳側有純謂之綼，裳下有純謂之裼，純者緣也。

translations.literal: When the skirt's sides had a border it was called side-edging; when below the skirt there was a border it was called hem-edging; border means edging.
translations.idiomatic: A border along the skirt's sides was called side-edging; a border below the skirt was called hem-edging—the term border here means edging.

translations.literal: The inner robe was made of plain gauze.
translations.idiomatic: The inner robe was made of plain gauze.

translations.literal: Green collar, cuffs, edging, and hem; the collar woven with thirteen opposed-triangle designs.
translations.idiomatic: It had a green collar, cuffs, edging, and hem, with thirteen opposed-triangle motifs woven on the collar.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝隨裳色，四章，織藻、粉米、黼黻各二。

translations.literal: The knee cover followed the skirt's color, four emblems, woven with waterweed, millet grain, axe-and-gouge, and opposed triangles, two each.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover matched the skirt in color and bore four emblems—waterweed, millet grain, axe-and-gouge, and opposed triangles, two of each.

sentences.zh: 本色緣，有紃，施於縫中。

translations.literal: Proper-color edging; there were cords set within the seams.
translations.idiomatic: It had edging in the proper colors and cords worked into the seams.

translations.literal: Two jade hooks.
translations.idiomatic: There were two jade hooks.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年，諭閣臣張璁：「袞冕有革帶，今何不用？

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing, the emperor instructed Grand Secretary Zhang Cong: "The sacrificial crown and robe include a leather belt — why is it not used now?
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 8 (1529) the emperor instructed Grand Secretary Zhang Cong, "The ceremonial crown and robe include a leather belt—why is it no longer used?

sentences.zh: 」璁對曰：「按陳祥道《禮書》，古革帶、大帶，皆謂之鞶。

translations.literal: " Cong replied: "According to Chen Xiangdao's Book of Rites, in antiquity the leather belt and great belt were both called the sash-girdle.
translations.idiomatic: " Cong replied, "According to Chen Xiangdao's Book of Rites, in antiquity the leather belt and the great belt were both called the sash-girdle.

sentences.zh: 革帶以纛佩韍，然後加以大帶，而笏搢於二帶之間。

translations.literal: The leather belt was used to hang pennants, pendants, and knee covers; only then was the great belt added, and the tablet inserted between the two belts.
translations.idiomatic: The leather belt carried pennants, pendants, and knee covers; only then was the great belt added, with the tablet tucked between the two belts.

sentences.zh: 夫革帶前系韍，後系綬，左右系佩，自古冕弁恆用之。

translations.literal: The leather belt attached knee covers in front, the sash behind, and pendants to left and right; from antiquity it was constantly used with the ceremonial crown and cap.
translations.idiomatic: The leather belt fastened knee covers in front, the ceremonial sash behind, and pendants to either side; from antiquity it was always worn with the ceremonial crown and cap.

sentences.zh: 今惟不用革帶，以至前後佩服皆無所繫，遂附屬裳要之間，失古制矣。

translations.literal: Now only by not using the leather belt, front and rear pendants and sash have nothing to which they can be attached, and so they are made to depend on the skirt's waist — this loses the ancient regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Today, because the leather belt is omitted, the front and rear pendants and sash have nothing to which they can be fastened and are merely attached at the skirt's waist, which departs from the ancient regulations.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「冕服祀天地，享祖宗，若闕革帶，非齊明盛服之意。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The court robes and crown sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and offer to the ancestors; if the leather belt is lacking, this is not the meaning of pure and splendid full dress.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The ceremonial robes are worn to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and to offer to the ancestors; to omit the leather belt is not in keeping with the intent of pure and splendid full dress.

sentences.zh: 及觀《會典》載蔽膝用羅，上織火、山、龍三章，並大帶緣用錦，皆與今所服不合。

translations.literal: Moreover, on examining the Collected Statutes, it records that the knee cover used gauze with fire, mountain, and dragon, three emblems woven above, and that the great belt's edging used brocade — all unlike what is worn today.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Collected Statutes record that the knee cover was gauze woven with the fire, mountain, and dragon emblems, and that the great belt's edging was brocade—all unlike what is worn today.

sentences.zh: 卿可並革帶系蔽膝、佩、綬之式，詳考繪圖以進。

translations.literal: You may together with the leather belt's manner of attaching knee cover, pendants, and sash, investigate in detail, draw illustrations, and submit them.
translations.idiomatic: You should also investigate in detail how the leather belt fastened the knee cover, pendants, and sash, draw illustrations, and submit them.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「衣裳分上下服，而今衣恆掩裳。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Upper garment and skirt are separate upper and lower dress, yet today the robe constantly covers the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "The upper garment and skirt are distinct upper and lower garments, yet today the robe constantly covers the skirt.

sentences.zh: 裳制如帷，而今兩幅。

translations.literal: The skirt's form should be like a curtain, yet today there are two panels.
translations.idiomatic: The skirt should be shaped like a curtain, yet today it is made in two panels.

sentences.zh: 朕意衣但當與裳要下齊，而露裳之六章，何如？

translations.literal: My idea is that the robe should only come level with the skirt's waist below, while revealing the skirt's six emblems — what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: My thought is that the robe should end only at the skirt's waist, leaving the skirt's six emblems visible—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 」已，又諭璁以變更祖制為疑。

translations.literal: " Thereafter he again instructed Cong, expressing doubt about altering the ancestral regulations.
translations.idiomatic: " Shortly afterward he again expressed to Cong his concern about altering the ancestral regulations.

sentences.zh: 璁對曰：「臣考禮制，衣不掩裳，與聖意允合。

translations.literal: Cong replied: "Your subject has examined the ritual regulations: the robe does not cover the skirt — this fully accords with Your Majesty's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Cong replied, "Your subject has examined the ritual regulations: the robe does not cover the skirt, which fully accords with Your Majesty's intent.

sentences.zh: 夫衣六章，裳六章，義各有取，衣自不容掩裳。

translations.literal: The robe has six emblems, the skirt six emblems; each has its own meaning — the robe by nature cannot cover the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: The robe bears six emblems and the skirt six, each with its own significance; the robe by its nature cannot cover the skirt.

sentences.zh: 《大明集禮》及《會典》與古制不異。

translations.literal: The Collected Rites of the Great Ming and the Collected Statutes do not differ from the ancient regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Collected Rites of the Great Ming and the Collected Statutes agree with the ancient regulations.

sentences.zh: 今衣八章，裳四章，故衣常掩裳，然於典籍無所準。

translations.literal: Now the robe has eight emblems and the skirt four, so the robe constantly covers the skirt — yet this has no basis in the canonical texts.
translations.idiomatic: Today the robe has eight emblems and the skirt four, so the robe constantly covers the skirt—yet this has no basis in the canonical texts.

sentences.zh: 內閣所藏圖注，蓋因官司織造，循習訛謬。

translations.literal: The illustrated commentaries kept in the Grand Secretariat were probably because the official workshops wove them, following corrupted practice.
translations.idiomatic: The illustrated commentaries kept in the Grand Secretariat probably reflect errors introduced when the official workshops wove the garments and followed corrupted practice.

sentences.zh: 今訂正之，乃復祖制，非有變更。

translations.literal: To correct this now is to restore the ancestral regulations, not to make a change.
translations.idiomatic: To correct this now is to restore the ancestral regulations, not to alter them.

sentences.zh: 」帝意乃決。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mind was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 因復諭璁曰：「衣有六章，古以繪，今當以織。

translations.literal: He then again instructed Cong: "The robe has six emblems; in antiquity they were painted — today they should be woven.
translations.idiomatic: He then again told Cong, "The robe has six emblems; in antiquity they were painted, but today they should be woven.

sentences.zh: 朕命織染局考國初冕服，日月各徑五寸，當從之。

translations.literal: I command the Weaving and Dyeing Bureau to examine the court robes and crown of the dynasty's founding; the sun and moon each had a diameter of five inches — this should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: I have ordered the Weaving and Dyeing Bureau to consult the founding-era court robes and crown: the sun and moon each measured five inches across, and that measure should be restored.

sentences.zh: 裳六章，古用繡，亦當從之。

translations.literal: The skirt had six emblems; antiquity used embroidery — this too should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The skirt bore six emblems, and in antiquity they were embroidered; that practice should be followed as well.

sentences.zh: 古色用玄黃，取象天地。

translations.literal: In antiquity the colors used were dark and yellow, taking the image of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the colors were dark and yellow, taking Heaven and Earth as their model.

sentences.zh: 今裳用纁，於義無取，當從古。

translations.literal: Today the skirt uses deep-red — in meaning there is nothing to be taken from this; we should follow antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Today the skirt is deep-red, which carries no proper symbolic meaning; we should return to the ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 革帶即束帶，後當用玉，以佩綬系之於下。

translations.literal: The leather belt is the waist belt; afterward jade should be used, with pendants and sash attached below it.
translations.idiomatic: The leather belt is the waist belt; jade should be used on it, with pendants and the ceremonial sash fastened below.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝隨裳色，其繡上龍下火，可不用山。

translations.literal: The knee cover follows the skirt's color; its embroidery has a dragon above and fire below — the mountain need not be used.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover should match the skirt in color, embroidered with a dragon above and fire below; the mountain emblem may be omitted.

sentences.zh: 卿與內閣諸臣同考之。

translations.literal: You and the various ministers of the Grand Secretariat should examine this together.
translations.idiomatic: You and the other ministers of the Grand Secretariat should investigate this together.

sentences.zh: 」於是楊一清等詳議：「袞冕之服，自黃、虞以來，玄衣黃裳，為十二章。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yang Yiqing and others deliberated in detail: "The sacrificial crown and robe, from the times of Huang and Yu, had a dark upper garment and yellow skirt, making twelve emblems.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Yang Yiqing and others submitted a detailed memorial: "The sacrificial crown and robe, from the age of Huang and Yu, consisted of a dark upper garment and yellow skirt bearing twelve emblems.

sentences.zh: 日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲，其序自上而下，為衣之六章；

translations.literal: Sun, moon, stars, mountain, dragon, and flowering creature — their order from top to bottom were the six emblems of the robe;
translations.idiomatic: The sun, moon, stars, mountain, dragon, and flowering creature, ordered from top to bottom, formed the robe's six emblems;

sentences.zh: 宗彝、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻，其序自下而上，為裳之六章。

translations.literal: ritual vessels, waterweed, fire, millet grain, axe-and-gouge, and opposed triangles — their order from bottom to top were the six emblems of the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: ritual vessels, waterweed, fire, millet grain, axe-and-gouge, and opposed triangles, ordered from bottom to top, formed the skirt's six emblems.

sentences.zh: 自周以後浸，變其制，或八章，或九章，已戾於古矣。

translations.literal: From Zhou onward they gradually changed the regulations, sometimes to eight emblems, sometimes nine — already departing from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhou onward the regulations were gradually altered, sometimes to eight emblems and sometimes to nine, already straying from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 我太祖皇帝復定為十二章之制，司造之官仍習舛訛，非製作之初意。

translations.literal: Our Founding Emperor restored the twelve-emblem regulation, but the officials who made them still followed corrupted errors — not the original intent of manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: Our Founding Emperor restored the twelve-emblem system, yet the workshops charged with production still followed corrupted practice, contrary to the original intent.

sentences.zh: 伏乞聖斷不疑。

translations.literal: We humbly beg Your Sacred judgment without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly beg Your Majesty to decide without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃令擇吉更正其制。

translations.literal: " The emperor then ordered an auspicious day chosen to correct the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then ordered an auspicious day chosen for correcting the regulations.

sentences.zh: 冠以圓匡烏紗冒之，旒綴七採玉珠十二，青纊充耳，綴玉珠二，餘如舊制。

translations.literal: The crown had a round frame covered with black gauze; the tassels strung twelve beads of seven colors; blue stuffing filled the ears, with two jade beads attached; the rest followed the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The crown had a round frame covered with black gauze; the tassels carried twelve beads in seven colors; blue stuffing filled the ears, with two jade beads attached; everything else followed the earlier regulations.

sentences.zh: 玄衣黃裳，衣裳各六章。

translations.literal: Dark upper garment, yellow skirt — robe and skirt each six emblems.
translations.idiomatic: There was a dark upper garment and a yellow skirt, the robe and skirt each bearing six emblems.

sentences.zh: 洪武間舊制，日月徑五寸，裳前後連屬如帷，六章用繡。

translations.literal: Under the Hongwu old regulations, sun and moon had a diameter of five inches; the skirt front and back were continuous like a curtain; the six emblems used embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old Hongwu regulations, the sun and moon measured five inches across; the skirt was joined front and back like a curtain, and the six emblems were embroidered.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝隨裳色，羅為之，上繡龍一，下繡火三，系於革帶，大帶素表朱裡，上緣以朱，下以綠。

translations.literal: The knee cover followed the skirt's color, made of gauze, one dragon embroidered above and three fires below, attached to the leather belt; the great belt was plain outside and vermilion inside, with vermilion edging above and green below.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover matched the skirt in color and was made of gauze, with one dragon embroidered above and three fires below, fastened to the leather belt; the great belt was plain outside and vermilion within, edged in vermilion above and green below.

sentences.zh: 革帶前用玉，其後無玉，以佩綬系而掩之。

translations.literal: The leather belt had jade in front but none behind; pendants and sash were fastened to cover it.
translations.idiomatic: The leather belt bore jade in front but not behind, with pendants and sash attached to cover the rear.

sentences.zh: 中單及圭，俱如永樂間制。

translations.literal: The inner robe and tablet were both as under the Yongle regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The inner robe and jade tablet both followed the Yongle regulations.

sentences.zh: 朱襪，赤舄，黃條緣玄纓結。

translations.literal: Vermilion stockings, red shoes, with yellow stripe edging and dark laces knotted.
translations.idiomatic: There were vermilion stockings and red court shoes, with yellow stripe edging and dark knotted laces.

sentences.zh: 皇帝通天冠服：洪武元年定，郊廟、省牲，皇太子諸王冠婚、醮戒，則服通天冠、絳紗袍。

translations.literal: The emperor's Communication-with-Heaven Cap dress: fixed in Hongwu 1; for suburban temples, inspecting sacrificial animals, crown prince and princes' capping and wedding, and fasting consecration, one wore the Communication-with-Heaven Cap and deep-red gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's Communication-with-Heaven Cap dress was fixed in Hongwu 1 (1368). For suburban temples, inspection of sacrificial animals, the crown prince's and princes' capping and wedding rites, and fasting consecration, he wore the Communication-with-Heaven Cap and a deep-red gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 冠加金博山，附蟬十二，首施珠翠，黑介幘，組纓，玉簪導。

translations.literal: The crown was topped with a gold Mount Bo, twelve cicadas attached, pearls and kingfisher feathers set on the front, a black cap covering, cord tassels, and a jade hairpin guide.
translations.idiomatic: The cap bore a gold Mount Bo ornament, twelve cicada pins, pearls and kingfisher feathers on the front, a black cap covering, cord tassels, and a jade hairpin guide.

sentences.zh: 絳紗袍，深衣制。

translations.literal: Deep-red gauze robe, in deep-garment style.
translations.idiomatic: The deep-red gauze robe followed the deep-garment cut.

sentences.zh: 白紗內單，皁領褾襈裾。

translations.literal: White gauze inner robe, with black collar, cuffs, edging, and hem.
translations.idiomatic: There was a white gauze inner robe with a black collar, cuffs, edging, and hem.

sentences.zh: 絳紗蔽膝，白假帶，方心曲領。

translations.literal: Deep-red gauze knee cover, white false belt, square heart and curved collar.
translations.idiomatic: There was a deep-red gauze knee cover, a white false belt, and a square-hearted curved collar.

sentences.zh: 白襪，赤舄。

translations.literal: White stockings, red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: White stockings and red court shoes completed the dress.

sentences.zh: 其革帶、佩綬，與袞服同。

translations.literal: Its leather belt and pendant sash were the same as for the sacrificial robe.
translations.idiomatic: The leather belt and pendant sash were the same as those worn with the sacrificial robe.

sentences.zh: 皇帝皮弁服：朔望視朝、降詔、降香、進表、四夷朝貢、外官朝覲、策士傳臚皆服之。

translations.literal: The emperor's leather cap (ceremonial) dress: on the new and full moon court audiences, issuing edicts, dispatching incense, presenting memorials, tribute from the four quarters, audiences of outer officials, and announcing the successful candidates at the imperial examination — all wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's leather cap (ceremonial) dress was worn for new- and full-moon court audiences, the promulgation of edicts, incense offerings, the presentation of memorials, tribute missions from the four quarters, audiences for outer officials, and the announcement of successful examination candidates.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖以後，祭太歲山川諸神亦服之。

translations.literal: After Jiajing, sacrifices to the Year Star, mountains, rivers, and various gods also used it.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiajing reign, it was also worn when sacrificing to the Year Star, mountains, rivers, and other deities.

sentences.zh: 其制自洪武二十六年定。

translations.literal: Its regulations were fixed in Hongwu 26.
translations.idiomatic: Its regulations were fixed in Hongwu 26 (1393).

sentences.zh: 皮弁用烏紗冒之，前後各十二縫，每縫綴五采玉十二以為飾，玉簪導，紅組纓。

translations.literal: The leather cap was covered with black gauze; front and back each had twelve seams, each seam strung with twelve five-colored jade ornaments; jade hairpin guide, red cord tassel.
translations.idiomatic: The leather cap was covered with black gauze and had twelve seams front and back; each seam carried twelve five-colored jade ornaments, with a jade hairpin guide and a red cord tassel.

sentences.zh: 其服絳紗衣，蔽膝隨衣色。

translations.literal: Its dress was a deep-red gauze robe; the knee cover followed the robe's color.
translations.idiomatic: The robe was of deep-red gauze, and the knee cover matched it in color.

sentences.zh: 白玉佩革帶。

translations.literal: White jade pendant leather belt.
translations.idiomatic: There was a leather belt with white jade pendants.

sentences.zh: 玉鉤苾，緋白大帶。

translations.literal: Jade hook plaques, crimson-and-white great belt.
translations.idiomatic: There were jade hook plaques and a great belt in crimson and white.

sentences.zh: 白襪，黑舄。

translations.literal: White stockings, black shoes.
translations.idiomatic: White stockings and black court shoes completed the dress.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年定，皮弁如舊制，惟縫及冠武並貫簪系纓處，皆飾以金玉。

translations.literal: Fixed in Yongle 3: the leather cap followed the old regulations, except that the seams, cap ridge, and the places where the hairpin passed and the tassel was tied were all ornamented with gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3 (1405) the leather cap was fixed as before, except that the seams, the cap ridge, and the points where the hairpin passed and the tassel was tied were all ornamented with gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 圭長如冕服之圭，有脊，並雙植文。

translations.literal: The tablet was as long as the court-robe tablet, had a ridge, and bore paired inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: The jade tablet matched the court-robe tablet in length, had a central ridge, and bore paired inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 絳紗袍，本色領褾襈裾。

translations.literal: Deep-red gauze robe, with collar, cuffs, edging, and hem in the proper colors.
translations.idiomatic: The deep-red gauze robe had a collar, cuffs, edging, and hem in the proper colors.

sentences.zh: 紅裳，但不織章數。

translations.literal: Red skirt, but without woven emblem count.
translations.idiomatic: There was a red skirt, but without the woven emblem count.

sentences.zh: 中單，紅領褾襈裾。

translations.literal: Inner robe, with red collar, cuffs, edging, and hem.
translations.idiomatic: The inner robe had a red collar, cuffs, edging, and hem.

sentences.zh: 餘俱如冕服內制。

translations.literal: The rest were all as the inner regulations of the court robes and crown.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed the inner dress regulations of the court robes and crown.

sentences.zh: 皇帝武弁服：明初親徵遣將服之。

translations.literal: The emperor's military cap dress: in early Ming, when the emperor personally campaigned or dispatched generals, he wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's military cap dress was worn in early Ming when the emperor took the field in person or dispatched generals on campaign.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年諭閣臣張璁云：「《會典》紀親徵、類禡之祭，皆具武弁服。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 8 the emperor instructed Grand Secretary Zhang Cong: "The Collected Statutes record that personal campaigns and pre-battle prayer sacrifices all require the military cap dress.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 8 (1529) the emperor instructed Grand Secretary Zhang Cong, "The Collected Statutes record that personal campaigns and pre-battle prayer sacrifices all require the military cap dress.

sentences.zh: 不可不備。

translations.literal: It cannot fail to be complete.
translations.idiomatic: It must be fully provided.

sentences.zh: 」璁對：《周禮》有韋弁，謂以韎韋為弁，又以為衣裳。

translations.literal: " Cong replied: The Rites of Zhou has the hide cap, meaning that crimson leather was used for the cap and also for the robe and skirt.
translations.idiomatic: " Cong replied: The Rites of Zhou describes the hide cap, by which crimson leather was used for the cap and also for the robe and skirt.

sentences.zh: 國朝視古損益，有皮弁之制。

translations.literal: Our dynasty, considering antiquity with additions and subtractions, has the leather cap (ceremonial) regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty, adapting ancient practice, already had regulations for the leather cap (ceremonial).

sentences.zh: 今武弁當如皮弁，但皮弁以黑紗冒之，武弁當以絳紗冒之。

translations.literal: Now the military cap should be like the leather cap, but the leather cap is covered with black gauze, whereas the military cap should be covered with deep-red gauze.
translations.idiomatic: The military cap should follow the leather cap (ceremonial), except that the leather cap is covered with black gauze while the military cap should be covered with deep-red gauze.

sentences.zh: 」隨具圖以進。

translations.literal: " He then submitted an illustrated plan.
translations.idiomatic: " He then submitted an illustrated plan.

translations.literal: The emperor replied: "On viewing the plan there is a knee-flap shape, but no place to attach it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The plan shows a knee-flap, but no place to fasten it.

sentences.zh: 冠制古象上尖，今皮弁則圓。

translations.literal: The crown regulations of antiquity imaged a pointed top; today's leather cap is round.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the cap was made with a pointed top; today's leather cap is round.

sentences.zh: 朕惟上銳取其輕利，當如古制。

translations.literal: I consider that the pointed top takes lightness and sharpness — it should follow the ancient regulations.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the pointed top was chosen for lightness and sharpness; the cap should follow the ancient form.

sentences.zh: 又衣裳韠舄皆赤色，何謂？

translations.literal: Also the robe, skirt, knee-flap, and shoes are all red — what is the meaning of this?
translations.idiomatic: And why are the robe, skirt, knee-flap, and shoes all red?

sentences.zh: 且佩綬俱無，於祭用之，可乎？

translations.literal: Moreover pendants and sash are entirely absent — for use in sacrifice, is this acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, there are no pendants or sash at all — is that acceptable for sacrificial use?

sentences.zh: 」璁對：「自古服冕弁俱用革帶，以前系韍，後系綬。

translations.idiomatic: " Cong replied, "From antiquity, ceremonial crowns and caps were always worn with a leather belt, the knee cover fastened in front and the sash behind.

sentences.zh: 韋弁之韠，正系於革帶耳。

translations.literal: The knee-flap of the hide cap was precisely attached to the leather belt.
translations.idiomatic: The hide cap's knee-flap was attached directly to the leather belt.

sentences.zh: 武事尚威烈，故色純用赤。

translations.literal: Military affairs esteem majesty and fierceness, so the colors purely use red.
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs emphasize awe and force, so the dress is entirely red.

sentences.zh: 」帝復報璁：「冠服、衣裳、韠舄俱如古制，增革帶、佩綬及圭。

translations.literal: " The emperor again replied to Cong: "The cap dress, robe, skirt, knee-flap, and shoes should all follow the ancient regulations, with the addition of leather belt, pendant sash, and tablet.

sentences.zh: 」乃定制，弁上銳，色用赤，上十二縫，中綴五采玉，落落如星狀。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the regulations were fixed: the cap was pointed on top, red in color, with twelve seams above, five-colored jade strung in the middle, scattered like stars.
translations.idiomatic: " The regulations were then fixed: the cap was pointed and red, with twelve seams on the upper part and five-colored jade strung between them, scattered like stars.

sentences.zh: 韎衣、韎裳、韎韐，俱赤色。

translations.literal: Crimson-leather robe, skirt, and leggings were all red.
translations.idiomatic: The crimson-leather robe, skirt, and leggings were all red.

sentences.zh: 佩、綬、革帶，如常制。

translations.literal: Pendants, sash, and leather belt followed the ordinary regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The pendants, sash, and leather belt followed the usual regulations.

sentences.zh: 佩綬及韎韐，俱上系於革帶。

translations.literal: Pendants, sash, and crimson leggings were all attached above to the leather belt.
translations.idiomatic: The pendants, sash, and crimson leggings were all fastened to the leather belt above.

sentences.zh: 舄如裳色。

translations.literal: Shoes matched the skirt's color.
translations.idiomatic: The shoes matched the skirt in color.

sentences.zh: 玉圭視鎮圭差小，剡上方下，有篆文曰：「討罪安民」。

translations.idiomatic: The jade tablet was slightly smaller than the quarter-tablet, square at the top and tapered below, and bore seal-script characters reading, "Subdue crime and pacify the people."

sentences.zh: 皇帝常服：洪武三年定，烏紗折角向上巾，盤領窄袖袍，束帶間用金、琥珀、透犀。

translations.literal: The emperor's daily dress: fixed in Hongwu 3 — black gauze cap with corners folded upward, round-collar narrow-sleeved robe, waist belt sometimes using gold, amber, and transparent rhinoceros horn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's daily dress was fixed in Hongwu 3 (1370): a black gauze cap with upturned corners, a round-collared narrow-sleeved robe, and a waist belt sometimes set with gold, amber, and transparent rhinoceros horn.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年更定，冠以烏紗冒之，折角向上，其後名翼善冠。

translations.literal: Revised in Yongle 3: the cap was covered with black gauze with corners folded upward; afterward it was named the Beneficent-Wing Cap.
translations.idiomatic: It was revised in Yongle 3 (1405): the cap was covered with black gauze and folded upward at the corners, and afterward was named the Beneficent-Wing Cap.

sentences.zh: 袍黃，盤領，窄袖，前後及兩肩各織金盤龍一。

translations.literal: The robe was yellow, round-collared and narrow-sleeved; front, back, and both shoulders each had one gold coiled dragon woven.
translations.idiomatic: The robe was yellow, with a round collar and narrow sleeves; one gold coiled dragon was woven on the front, back, and each shoulder.

sentences.zh: 帶用玉，靴以皮為之。

translations.literal: The belt used jade; boots were made of leather.
translations.idiomatic: The belt was of jade, and the boots were leather.

sentences.zh: 先是，洪武二十四年，帝微行至神樂觀，見有結網巾者。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Hongwu 24, the emperor went incognito to the Divine Music Observatory and saw someone wearing a net cap.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Hongwu 24 (1391), the emperor went incognito to the Divine Music Observatory and saw a man wearing a net cap.

sentences.zh: 翼日，命取網巾，頒示十三布政使司，人無貴賤，皆裹網巾，於是天子亦常服網巾。

translations.literal: The next day he ordered net caps taken and issued to the thirteen provincial administrative commissions; people without distinction of noble or base all wrapped net caps — thus the Son of Heaven also wore a net cap as daily dress.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he ordered net caps collected and issued to the thirteen provincial commissions; thereafter men of every rank wore them, and the Son of Heaven adopted the net cap as part of his daily dress as well.

sentences.zh: 又《會典》載皇太孫冠禮有云：「掌冠跪加網巾」，而皇帝、皇太子冠服，俱闕而不載。

translations.literal: Also the Collected Statutes record the imperial great-grandson's capping rite as saying, "The cap officer kneels and adds the net cap," yet the crown dress of the emperor and crown prince are both omitted and not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The Collected Statutes also record, in the imperial great-grandson's capping rite, that "the cap officer kneels and sets the net cap in place," yet the capping dress of the emperor and crown prince is nowhere recorded.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年，更定燕弁服。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 7 the casual court cap dress was revised.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 7 (1528) the casual court cap dress was revised.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以燕居冠服，尚沿習俗，諭張璁考古帝王燕居法服之制。

translations.literal: Initially, because the emperor's dress for private residence still followed custom, he instructed Zhang Cong to examine the ancient regulations for emperors' ritual dress at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: At first, finding that the emperor's dress for private residence still followed ordinary custom, he instructed Zhang Cong to investigate how ancient emperors dressed for ritual occasions at leisure.

sentences.zh: 璁乃採《禮書》「玄端深衣。

translations.literal: Cong then adopted from the Book of Rites the passage, "Dark robe and deep garment.
translations.idiomatic: Cong then drew from the Book of Rites the passage, "Dark robe and deep garment.

sentences.zh: 」之文，圖注以進。

translations.literal: " and submitted an illustrated commentary.
translations.idiomatic: " and submitted it with illustrated commentary.

sentences.zh: 帝為參定其制，諭璁詳議。

translations.literal: The emperor had him determine the regulations and instructed Cong to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him work out the regulations and instructed Cong to submit a detailed proposal.

sentences.zh: 璁言：「古者冕服之外，玄端深衣，其用最廣。

translations.literal: Cong said: "In antiquity, beyond the court robes and crown, the dark robe and deep garment had the widest use.
translations.idiomatic: Cong said, "In antiquity, apart from the court robes and crown, the dark robe and deep garment were the most widely worn garments.

sentences.zh: 玄端自天子達於士，國家之命服也。

translations.literal: The dark robe extended from the Son of Heaven down to the scholar — it was the state's mandated dress.
translations.idiomatic: The dark robe extended from the Son of Heaven down to the scholar; it was the dress mandated by the state.

sentences.zh: 深衣自天子達於庶人，聖賢之法服也。

translations.literal: The deep garment extended from the Son of Heaven down to the commoner — it was the sages' ritual dress.
translations.idiomatic: The deep garment extended from the Son of Heaven down to the commoner; it was the ritual dress of the sages.

sentences.zh: 今以玄端加文飾，不易舊制，深衣易黃色，不離中衣，誠得帝王損益時中之道。

translations.literal: Now to use the dark robe with added decorative patterns without changing the old regulations, and to change the deep garment to yellow without departing from the inner robe — truly this attains the emperors' way of additions and subtractions at the timely mean.
translations.idiomatic: To adorn the dark robe without abandoning the old form, and to make the deep garment yellow while keeping the inner robe unchanged, truly captures the emperor's way of adapting ancient practice to the proper mean.

sentences.zh: 」帝因諭禮部曰：「古玄端上下通用，今非古人比，雖燕居，宜辨等威。

translations.literal: " The emperor therefore instructed the Ministry of Rites: "In antiquity the dark robe was used alike above and below; today we are not comparable to the men of antiquity — even in private residence, ranks and authority should be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor therefore instructed the Ministry of Rites, "In antiquity the dark robe was worn alike by high and low, but we are not the ancients; even in private residence, rank and dignity should be preserved.

sentences.zh: 」因酌古制，更名曰：「燕弁」，寓深宮獨處、以燕安為戒之意。

translations.literal: " Accordingly considering the ancient regulations, the name was revised to: "Casual Court Cap," conveying the meaning of dwelling alone in the inner palace and taking ease and restraint as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: " Accordingly, drawing on ancient practice, the dress was renamed the "Casual Court Cap," expressing the idea of dwelling alone within the inner palace and taking repose and restraint as a warning.

sentences.zh: 其制，冠匡如皮弁之制，冒以烏紗，分十有二瓣，各以金線壓之，前飾五采玉雲各一，後列四山，朱條為組纓，雙玉簪。

translations.literal: Its regulations: the cap frame followed the leather cap (ceremonial) form, covered with black gauze and divided into twelve petals, each pressed with gold thread; the front bore one five-colored jade cloud each, the rear arrayed four mountains; vermilion cords served as tassels, with double jade hairpins.
translations.idiomatic: Its regulations were as follows: the cap frame followed the leather cap (ceremonial), covered with black gauze and divided into twelve petals, each traced with gold thread; the front bore one five-colored jade cloud on each side, the rear four mountain ornaments, vermilion cord tassels, and two jade hairpins.

sentences.zh: 服如古玄端之制，色玄，邊緣以青，兩肩繡日月，前盤圓龍一，後盤方龍二，邊加龍文八十一，領與兩祛共龍文五九。

translations.literal: The dress followed the ancient dark robe: dark in color with green edging; both shoulders embroidered with sun and moon; one coiled round dragon in front and two coiled square dragons behind; the border added eighty-one dragon designs; collar and both sleeves together had fifty-nine dragon designs.
translations.idiomatic: The robe followed the ancient dark robe: dark in color with green edging; the shoulders bore embroidered sun and moon; one coiled round dragon appeared in front and two coiled square dragons behind; the border carried eighty-one dragon motifs, and the collar and both sleeves together fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 衽同前後齊，共龍文四九。

translations.literal: The lapel was level front and back alike, with forty-nine dragon designs in all.
translations.idiomatic: The lapel was even front and back, with forty-nine dragon motifs in all.

sentences.zh: 襯用深衣之制，色黃。

translations.literal: The lining followed the deep-garment regulations, yellow in color.
translations.idiomatic: The lining followed the deep-garment cut and was yellow.

sentences.zh: 袂圓祛方，下齊負繩及踝十二幅。

translations.literal: Sleeves were round and cuffs square; the lower hem carried cords and twelve panels reaching the ankle.
translations.idiomatic: The sleeves were round and the cuffs square; the lower hem had tie cords and twelve panels reaching the ankle.

sentences.zh: 素帶，朱裡青表，綠緣邊，腰圍飾以玉龍九。

translations.literal: Plain belt, vermilion inside and green outside, with green edging; the waist was ornamented with nine jade dragons.
translations.idiomatic: There was a plain belt, vermilion within and green without, with green edging, and the waist was ornamented with nine jade dragons.

sentences.zh: 玄履，朱緣紅纓黃結。

translations.literal: Dark shoes, with vermilion edging, red tassels, and yellow knots.
translations.idiomatic: Dark shoes had vermilion edging, red tassels, and yellow knots.

sentences.zh: 白襪。

translations.literal: White stockings.
translations.idiomatic: White stockings completed the dress.

sentences.zh: 皇后冠服：洪武三年定，受冊、謁廟、朝會，服禮服。

translations.literal: The empress's crown and dress: fixed in Hongwu 3; upon receiving investiture, visiting the temple, and at court assemblies, she wore ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's crown and dress were fixed in Hongwu 3 (1370). Upon receiving investiture, visiting the ancestral temple, and attending court assemblies, she wore full ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 其冠圓匡，冒以翡翠，上飾九龍四鳳，大花十二樹，小花數如之。

translations.literal: Her crown had a round frame covered with kingfisher feathers, ornamented above with nine dragons and four phoenixes, twelve great floral sprays, and small flowers in the same number.
translations.idiomatic: Her crown had a round frame covered with kingfisher feathers and ornamented with nine dragons and four phoenixes above, twelve large floral sprays, and the same number of smaller flowers.

sentences.zh: 兩博鬢十二鈿。

translations.literal: Both wide temple tresses had twelve hairpin ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Both wide temple tresses bore twelve hairpin ornaments.

sentences.zh: 禕衣，深青繪翟，赤質，五色十二等。

translations.literal: Ceremonial robe, deep blue with painted pheasants, red ground, twelve grades in five colors.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial robe was deep blue with painted pheasants on a red ground, in twelve grades of five colors.

sentences.zh: 素紗中單，黻領，朱羅縠逯襈裾。

translations.literal: Plain gauze inner robe, opposed-triangle collar, vermilion gauze with patterned weave on edging and hem.
translations.idiomatic: There was a plain gauze inner robe with an opposed-triangle collar and vermilion gauze with patterned weave on the edging and hem.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝隨衣色，以緅為領緣，用翟為章三等。

translations.literal: The knee cover followed the robe's color, using dark crimson for collar edging, with pheasant emblems in three grades.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover matched the robe in color, with dark-crimson collar edging and pheasant emblems in three grades.

sentences.zh: 大帶隨衣色，朱裡紕其外，上以朱錦，下以綠錦，紐約用青組。

translations.literal: The great belt followed the robe's color, vermilion inside and bordered outside; vermilion brocade above and green brocade below; knot fasteners used green cords.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt matched the robe in color, vermilion within and bordered without, with vermilion brocade above and green brocade below, and green cord fasteners.

sentences.zh: 玉革帶。

translations.literal: Jade leather belt.
translations.idiomatic: There was a jade-set leather belt.

sentences.zh: 青襪、青舄，以金飾。

translations.literal: Green stockings and green shoes, ornamented with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Green stockings and green court shoes, ornamented with gold.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年定制，其冠飾翠龍九，金鳳四，中一龍銜大珠一，上有翠蓋，下垂珠結，餘皆口銜珠滴，珠翠雲四十片，大珠花、小珠花數如舊。

translations.literal: Regulations fixed in Yongle 3: the crown was ornamented with nine kingfisher dragons and four gold phoenixes; the middle dragon held one great pearl, with a kingfisher canopy above and hanging pearl knots below; the rest all held pearl drops in the mouth; forty pieces of pearl-and-kingfisher cloud; great pearl flowers and small pearl flowers in numbers as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3 (1405) the regulations were revised: the crown bore nine kingfisher dragons and four gold phoenixes; the central dragon held a great pearl beneath a kingfisher canopy, with pearl knots hanging below; the rest all held pearl drops in their mouths; there were forty pearl-and-kingfisher cloud pieces, with great and small pearl flowers in the same numbers as before.

sentences.zh: 三博鬢，飾以金龍、翠雲，皆垂珠滴。

translations.literal: Three wide temple tresses, ornamented with gold dragons and kingfisher clouds, all with hanging pearl drops.
translations.idiomatic: Three wide temple tresses were ornamented with gold dragons and kingfisher clouds, each hung with pearl drops.

sentences.zh: 翠口圈一副，上飾珠寶鈿花十二，翠鈿如其數。

translations.literal: One kingfisher mouth ring, ornamented above with twelve pearl-and-gem hairpin flowers, with kingfisher hairpin ornaments in the same number.
translations.idiomatic: There was one kingfisher mouth ring, set above with twelve pearl-and-gem floral hairpins and the same number of kingfisher hairpin ornaments.

sentences.zh: 託裡金口圈一副。

translations.literal: One gold mouth ring with backing.
translations.idiomatic: There was one gold mouth ring with a backing piece.

sentences.zh: 珠翠面花五事。

translations.literal: Five pearl-and-kingfisher face flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Five pearl-and-kingfisher forehead ornaments completed the set.

sentences.zh: 珠排環一對。

translations.literal: One pair of pearl strand rings.
translations.idiomatic: There was one pair of pearl strand rings.

sentences.zh: 皁羅額子一，描金龍文，用珠二十一。

translations.literal: One black gauze forehead band, with gold-traced dragon designs, using twenty-one pearls.
translations.idiomatic: A black gauze forehead band bore gold-traced dragon motifs and was set with twenty-one pearls.

sentences.zh: 翟衣，深青，織翟文十有二等，間以小輪花。

translations.literal: Pheasant robe, deep blue, woven with pheasant designs in twelve grades, interspersed with small wheel flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The pheasant robe was deep blue, woven with pheasant motifs in twelve grades and interspersed with small wheel flowers.

sentences.zh: 紅領褾襈裾，織金雲龍文。

translations.literal: Red collar, cuffs, edging, and hem, woven with gold cloud-and-dragon designs.
translations.idiomatic: It had a red collar, cuffs, edging, and hem, woven with gold cloud-and-dragon motifs.

sentences.zh: 中單，玉色紗為之，紅領褾襈裾，織黻文十三。

translations.literal: Inner robe made of jade-colored gauze, with red collar, cuffs, edging, and hem, and thirteen opposed-triangle designs woven on the collar.
translations.idiomatic: The inner robe was jade-colored gauze with a red collar, cuffs, edging, and hem, and thirteen opposed-triangle motifs on the collar.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝隨衣色，織翟為章三等，間以小輪花四，以緅為領緣，織金雲龍文。

translations.literal: The knee cover followed the robe's color, with pheasants woven as emblems in three grades, four small wheel flowers interspersed, dark-crimson collar edging, and gold cloud-and-dragon designs woven on it.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover matched the robe in color and bore pheasant emblems in three grades, four interspersed small wheel flowers, dark-crimson collar edging, and woven gold cloud-and-dragon motifs.

sentences.zh: 玉穀圭，長七寸，剡其上，瑑谷文，黃綺約其下，韜以黃囊，金龍文。

translations.literal: Jade grain-pattern tablet, seven inches long, its upper part tapered, carved with grain designs, bound below with yellow gauze, sheathed in a yellow pouch with gold dragon designs.
translations.idiomatic: The jade tablet bore a grain pattern, measured seven inches, was tapered at the top and carved with grain motifs, bound below with yellow gauze, and sheathed in a yellow pouch embroidered with gold dragons.

sentences.zh: 玉革帶，青綺鞓，描金雲龍文，玉事件十，金事件四。

translations.literal: Jade leather belt, green gauze strap with gold-traced cloud-and-dragon designs, ten jade fittings and four gold fittings.
translations.idiomatic: There was a jade-set leather belt with a green gauze strap traced in gold with cloud-and-dragon motifs, ten jade fittings, and four gold fittings.

sentences.zh: 大帶，表裡俱青紅相半，末純紅，下垂織金雲龍文，上朱緣，下綠緣，青綺副帶一。

translations.literal: Great belt, outer and inner both half green and half red, the end purely red, the lower hanging portion woven with gold cloud-and-dragon designs, vermilion edging above and green edging below, and one supplementary belt of green gauze.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt was green and red in equal halves inside and out, purely red at the tip, with the lower hanging portion woven in gold cloud-and-dragon motifs, vermilion edging above, green edging below, and one supplementary green gauze belt.

sentences.zh: 綬五采，黃、赤、白、縹、綠，纁質，間施二玉環，皆織成。

translations.literal: Five-colored sash—yellow, red, white, pale crimson, and green—of deep-red thread, with two jade rings set between, all woven complete.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial sash used five colors—yellow, red, white, pale crimson, and green—on deep-red thread, with two jade rings spaced along it, all fully woven.

sentences.zh: 小綬三，色同大綬。

translations.literal: Three small sashes, colors the same as the great sash.
translations.idiomatic: Three smaller sashes matched the colors of the great sash.

sentences.zh: 玉佩二，各用玉珩一、瑀一、琚二、沖牙一、璜二，瑀下垂玉花一、玉滴二；

translations.literal: Two jade pendants, each using one top bar, one secondary piece, two square plaques, one impact tooth, and two arc pieces; from the secondary piece hung one jade blossom and two jade drops;
translations.idiomatic: There were two jade pendants, each comprising one top bar, one secondary piece, two square plaques, one impact tooth, and two arc pieces; from the secondary piece hung one jade blossom and two jade drops;

sentences.zh: 瑑飾雲龍文描金；

translations.literal: carved ornament with cloud-and-dragon designs traced in gold;
translations.idiomatic: they were carved with cloud-and-dragon motifs and traced in gold;

sentences.zh: 自珩而下，系組五，貫以玉珠，行則沖牙二滴與二璜相觸有聲；

translations.literal: from the top bar downward five cords were attached, strung with jade beads; when walking, the impact tooth, two drops, and two arc pieces struck one another and made a sound;
translations.idiomatic: below the top bar five cords were fastened, strung with jade beads; when the wearer walked, the impact tooth, the two drops, and the two arc pieces chimed against one another;

sentences.zh: 上有金鉤，有小綬五采以副之，纁質，織成。

translations.literal: above there were gold hooks, with a small five-colored sash as supplement, of deep-red thread, woven complete.
translations.idiomatic: gold hooks were fitted above, supplemented by a small five-colored sash of deep-red thread, fully woven.

sentences.zh: 青襪舄，飾以描金雲龍，皁純，每舄首加珠五顆。

translations.literal: Green stockings and court shoes, ornamented with gold-traced cloud-and-dragons, black edging, five pearls added to each shoe toe.
translations.idiomatic: Green stockings and court shoes bore gold-traced cloud-and-dragon ornament, black trim, and five pearls on each toe.

sentences.zh: 皇后常服：洪武三年定，雙鳳翊龍冠，首飾、釧鐲用金玉、珠寶、翡翠。

translations.literal: The empress's everyday dress: fixed in Hongwu 3, Twin-Phoenix Flanking Dragon Crown; head ornaments, bracelets, and bangles used gold, jade, pearls, gems, and kingfisher.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's everyday dress was fixed in Hongwu 3 (1370): the Twin-Phoenix Flanking Dragon Crown, with head ornaments, bracelets, and bangles of gold, jade, pearls, gems, and kingfisher.

sentences.zh: 諸色團衫，金繡龍鳳文，帶用金玉。

translations.literal: Round-collared jackets in various colors, gold-embroidered with dragon-and-phoenix designs; the belt used gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: She wore round-collared jackets in various colors embroidered in gold with dragon-and-phoenix motifs, with a belt of gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 四年更定，龍鳳珠翠冠，真紅大袖衣霞帔，紅羅長裙，紅褙子。

translations.literal: Revised in the fourth year: Dragon-and-Phoenix Pearl-and-Kingfisher Crown, true-red large-sleeved robe with cloud collar, red gauze long skirt, and red over-jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the dress was revised to the Dragon-and-Phoenix Pearl-and-Kingfisher Crown, a true-red large-sleeved robe with cloud collar, a red gauze long skirt, and a red over-jacket.

sentences.zh: 冠制如特髻，上加龍鳳飾，衣用織金龍鳳文，加繡飾。

translations.literal: The crown followed the special-topknot form, with dragon-and-phoenix ornament added above; the robe used woven gold dragon-and-phoenix designs with added embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: The crown followed the special-topknot form topped with dragon-and-phoenix ornament, and the robe bore woven-gold dragon-and-phoenix motifs with added embroidery.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年更定，冠用皁縠，附以翠博山，上飾金龍一，翊以珠。

translations.literal: Revised again in Yongle 3: the crown used black gauze, with a kingfisher Mount Bo attached, ornamented above with one gold dragon flanked by pearls.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3 (1405) it was revised again: the crown was black gauze with an attached kingfisher Mount Bo, bearing one gold dragon above flanked by pearls.

sentences.zh: 翠鳳二，皆口銜珠滴。

translations.literal: Two kingfisher phoenixes, all holding pearl drops in the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Two kingfisher phoenixes, each holding a pearl drop in its mouth.

sentences.zh: 前後珠牡丹二，花八蕊，翠葉三十六。

translations.literal: Two pearl peonies before and behind, eight stamens to each flower, thirty-six kingfisher leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Before and behind were two pearl peonies of eight stamens each and thirty-six kingfisher leaves.

sentences.zh: 珠翠穰花鬢二，珠翠雲二十一，翠口圈一。

translations.literal: Two pearl-and-kingfisher cluster-flower temple tresses, twenty-one pearl-and-kingfisher clouds, one kingfisher mouth ring.
translations.idiomatic: There were two pearl-and-kingfisher cluster-flower temple tresses, twenty-one pearl-and-kingfisher cloud pieces, and one kingfisher mouth ring.

sentences.zh: 金寶鈿花九，飾以珠。

translations.literal: Nine gold-and-gem hairpin flowers, ornamented with pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Nine gold-and-gem floral hairpins were set with pearls.

sentences.zh: 金鳳二，口銜珠結。

translations.literal: Two gold phoenixes, holding pearl knots in the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Two gold phoenixes held pearl knots in their mouths.

sentences.zh: 三博鬢，飾以鸞鳳。

translations.literal: Three wide temple tresses, ornamented with luan-birds and phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Three wide temple tresses were ornamented with luan-birds and phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 金寶鈿二十四，邊垂珠滴。

translations.literal: Twenty-four gold-and-gem hairpin ornaments, with pearl drops hanging from the edges.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four gold-and-gem hairpin ornaments hung pearl drops from their edges.

sentences.zh: 金簪二。

translations.literal: Two gold hairpins.
translations.idiomatic: Two gold hairpins completed the set.

sentences.zh: 珊瑚鳳冠觜一副。

translations.literal: One coral phoenix crown beak-piece.
translations.idiomatic: There was one coral phoenix crown beak-piece.

sentences.zh: 大衫霞帔，衫黃，霞帔深青，織金雲霞龍文，或繡或鋪翠圈金，飾以珠玉墜子，瑑龍文。

translations.literal: Great robe and cloud collar: the robe yellow, the cloud collar deep blue, woven with gold cloud, mist, and dragon designs, or embroidered or appliquéd with kingfisher circled in gold, ornamented with pearl-and-jade pendants, carved with dragon designs.
translations.idiomatic: The great robe was yellow and the cloud collar deep blue, woven in gold with cloud, mist, and dragon motifs—or embroidered or appliquéd with kingfisher circled in gold—ornamented with pearl-and-jade pendants and carved with dragon designs.

sentences.zh: 四衤癸襖子，

translations.literal: Four-panel over-jacket,
translations.idiomatic: A four-panel over-jacket,

translations.literal: open bracket

sentences.zh: （即褙子。）〉

translations.literal: (That is, the over-jacket.)〉
translations.idiomatic: that is, the over-jacket.)

sentences.zh: 深青，金繡團龍文。

translations.literal: deep blue, gold-embroidered with coiled dragon roundels.
translations.idiomatic: deep blue and gold-embroidered with coiled dragon roundels.

sentences.zh: 鞠衣紅色，前後織金雲龍文，或繡或鋪翠圈金，飾以珠。

translations.literal: Ju robe in red, front and back woven with gold cloud-and-dragon designs, or embroidered or appliquéd with kingfisher circled in gold, ornamented with pearls.
translations.idiomatic: The ju robe was red, with gold cloud-and-dragon motifs woven front and back—or embroidered or appliquéd with kingfisher circled in gold—and set with pearls.

sentences.zh: 大帶紅線羅為之，有緣，餘或青或綠，各隨鞠衣色。

translations.literal: The great belt was made of red-thread gauze, with edging; the rest might be blue or green, each following the ju robe's color.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt was red-thread gauze with edging; the remaining portions were blue or green according to the color of the ju robe.

sentences.zh: 緣襈襖子，黃色，紅領褾襈裾，皆織金采色雲龍文。

translations.literal: Bordered jacket, yellow, with red collar, cuffs, edging, and hem, all woven with gold multicolored cloud-and-dragon designs.
translations.idiomatic: The bordered jacket was yellow with a red collar, cuffs, edging, and hem, all woven in gold with multicolored cloud-and-dragon motifs.

sentences.zh: 緣襈裙，紅色，綠緣襈，織金采色雲龍文。

translations.literal: Bordered skirt, red, with green edging and border, woven with gold multicolored cloud-and-dragon designs.
translations.idiomatic: The bordered skirt was red with green edging and border, woven in gold with multicolored cloud-and-dragon motifs.

sentences.zh: 玉帶，如翟衣內制，第減金事件一。

translations.literal: Jade belt, as under the pheasant-robe inner regulations, but with one gold fitting removed.
translations.idiomatic: The jade belt followed the inner regulations of the pheasant robe, but with one gold fitting omitted.

sentences.zh: 玉花采結綬，以紅綠線羅為結，玉綬花一，瑑雲龍文。

translations.literal: Jade-flower colored-knot sash, the knot made of red-and-green thread gauze, one jade sash flower, carved with cloud-and-dragon designs.
translations.idiomatic: The jade-flower colored-knot sash used a red-and-green thread gauze knot, with one jade sash flower carved in cloud-and-dragon motif.

sentences.zh: 綬帶玉墜珠六，金垂頭花瓣四，小金葉六。

translations.literal: On the sash belt: six jade pendants and pearls, four gold hanging petal ornaments, six small gold leaves.
translations.idiomatic: The sash belt bore six jade pendants and pearls, four gold hanging petal ornaments, and six small gold leaves.

sentences.zh: 紅線羅系帶一。

translations.literal: One red-thread gauze tie belt.
translations.idiomatic: A red-thread gauze tie belt completed the set.

sentences.zh: 白玉雲樣玎榼二，如佩制，有金鉤，金如意雲蓋一，下懸紅組五貫，金方心雲板一，俱鈒雲龍文，襯以紅綺，下垂金長頭花四，中小金鐘一，末綴白玉雲朵五。

translations.literal: Two white jade cloud-shaped tinkling ornaments, as per pendant regulations, with gold hooks; one gold ruyi cloud canopy, below which hung five strands of red cord; one gold square-hearted cloud plaque, all inlaid with cloud-and-dragon designs, lined with red gauze; below hung four gold long-headed flowers, one small gold bell among them, and five white jade cloud pieces at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Two white jade cloud-shaped tinklers followed pendant regulations and bore gold hooks; one gold ruyi cloud canopy hung below on five strands of red cord, with one gold square-hearted cloud plaque—all inlaid with cloud-and-dragon designs and lined with red gauze; below hung four gold long-headed flowers with a small gold bell among them, and five white jade cloud pieces at the end.

sentences.zh: 青襪舄，與翟衣內制同。

translations.literal: Green stockings and court shoes, the same as under the pheasant-robe inner regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Green stockings and court shoes matched the inner regulations of the pheasant robe.

sentences.zh: 皇妃、皇嬪及內命婦冠服：洪武三年定，皇妃受冊、助祭、朝會禮服。

translations.literal: Crowns and dress of imperial consorts, imperial concubines, and inner-court titled ladies: fixed in Hongwu 3; the imperial consort's ceremonial dress for receiving investiture, assisting at sacrifices, and court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: The crowns and dress of imperial consorts, imperial concubines, and inner-court titled ladies were fixed in Hongwu 3 (1370). For receiving investiture, assisting at sacrifices, and attending court assemblies, the imperial consort wore full ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 冠飾九翬、四鳳花釵九樹，小花數如之。

translations.literal: The crown was ornamented with nine pheasant plumes and four phoenixes; nine floral hairpin sprays, with small flowers in the same number.
translations.idiomatic: The crown bore nine pheasant plumes and four phoenixes, nine floral hairpin sprays, and the same number of smaller flowers.

sentences.zh: 兩博鬢九鈿。

translations.literal: Both wide temple tresses had nine hairpin ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Both wide temple tresses bore nine hairpin ornaments.

sentences.zh: 翟衣，青質繡翟，編次於衣及裳，重為九等。

translations.literal: Pheasant robe, blue ground embroidered with pheasants, arranged in sequence on robe and skirt, layered in nine grades.
translations.idiomatic: The pheasant robe had a blue ground embroidered with pheasants arranged in sequence on robe and skirt in nine grades.

sentences.zh: 青紗中單，黻領，朱縠逯襈裾。

translations.literal: Blue gauze inner robe, opposed-triangle collar, vermilion gauze with patterned weave on edging and hem.
translations.idiomatic: There was a blue gauze inner robe with an opposed-triangle collar and vermilion gauze with patterned weave on the edging and hem.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝隨裳色，加文繡重雉，為章二等，以緅為領緣。

translations.literal: The knee cover followed the skirt's color, with added embroidered double pheasants as emblems in two grades, dark-crimson collar edging.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover matched the skirt in color, bore added embroidered double-pheasant emblems in two grades, and had dark-crimson collar edging.

sentences.zh: 大帶隨衣色。

translations.literal: The great belt followed the robe's color.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt matched the robe in color.

sentences.zh: 玉革帶。

translations.literal: Jade leather belt.
translations.idiomatic: There was a jade-set leather belt.

sentences.zh: 青襪舄、佩綬。

translations.literal: Green stockings and court shoes, pendant sash.
translations.idiomatic: Green stockings and court shoes, with pendant sash, completed the dress.

sentences.zh: 常服：鸞鳳冠，首飾、釧鐲用金玉、珠寶、翠。

translations.literal: Everyday dress: Luan-and-Phoenix Crown; head ornaments, bracelets, and bangles used gold, jade, pearls, gems, and kingfisher.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress comprised the Luan-and-Phoenix Crown, with head ornaments, bracelets, and bangles of gold, jade, pearls, gems, and kingfisher.

sentences.zh: 諸色團衫，金繡鸞鳳，不用黃。

translations.literal: Round-collared jackets in various colors, gold-embroidered with luan-birds and phoenixes; yellow was not used.
translations.idiomatic: Round-collared jackets in various colors were gold-embroidered with luan-birds and phoenixes, but yellow was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 帶用金、玉、犀。

translations.literal: The belt used gold, jade, and rhinoceros horn.
translations.idiomatic: The belt was of gold, jade, and rhinoceros horn.

sentences.zh: 又定山鬆特髻，假鬢花鈿，或花釵鳳冠。

translations.literal: Also fixed were the pine-mountain special topknot, false temple tresses with floral hairpin ornaments, or flower hairpins with phoenix crown.
translations.idiomatic: The pine-mountain special topknot was also prescribed, with false temple tresses and floral hairpin ornaments, or flower hairpins with a phoenix crown.

sentences.zh: 真紅大袖衣，霞帔，紅羅裙，褙子，衣用織金及繡鳳文。

translations.literal: True-red large-sleeved robe, cloud collar, red gauze skirt, over-jacket; the robe used woven gold and embroidered phoenix designs.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress included a true-red large-sleeved robe, cloud collar, red gauze skirt, and over-jacket, the robe bearing woven-gold and embroidered phoenix motifs.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年更定，禮服：九翟冠二，以皁縠為之，附以翠博山，飾大珠翟二，小珠翟三，翠翟四，皆口銜珠滴。

translations.literal: Revised again in Yongle 3, ceremonial dress: Nine-Pheasant Crown, made of black gauze, with kingfisher Mount Bo attached, ornamented with two large pearl pheasants, three small pearl pheasants, and four kingfisher pheasants, all holding pearl drops in the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3 (1405) ceremonial dress was revised again: the Nine-Pheasant Crown was black gauze with an attached kingfisher Mount Bo, bearing two large pearl pheasants, three small pearl pheasants, and four kingfisher pheasants, all holding pearl drops in their mouths.

sentences.zh: 冠中寶珠一座，翠頂雲一座，其珠牡丹、翠穰花鬢之屬，俱如雙鳳翊龍冠制，第減翠雲十。

translations.literal: One treasure pearl in the crown's center, one kingfisher summit cloud; pearl peonies, kingfisher cluster-flower temple tresses, and the like all followed the Twin-Phoenix Flanking Dragon Crown regulations, but with ten kingfisher clouds removed.
translations.idiomatic: The crown held one treasure pearl at its center and one kingfisher summit cloud; pearl peonies, kingfisher cluster-flower temple tresses, and the like all followed the Twin-Phoenix Flanking Dragon Crown, but with ten kingfisher clouds omitted.

sentences.zh: 又翠牡丹花、穰花各二，面花四，梅花環四，珠環各二。

translations.literal: Also two kingfisher peonies and two cluster flowers each, four face flowers, four plum-blossom rings, and two pearl rings each.
translations.idiomatic: There were also two kingfisher peonies and two cluster flowers each, four forehead flowers, four plum-blossom rings, and two pearl rings apiece.

sentences.zh: 其大衫、霞帔、燕居佩服之飾，俱同中宮，第織金繡瑑，俱雲霞鳳文，不用雲龍文。

translations.literal: The great robe, cloud collar, and private-residence sash and pendant ornaments all matched the empress's, but woven gold, embroidery, and carving all used cloud, mist, and phoenix designs, not cloud-and-dragon designs.
translations.idiomatic: The great robe, cloud collar, and private-residence sash and pendant ornaments all matched the empress's, but woven gold, embroidery, and carving bore cloud, mist, and phoenix motifs throughout—not cloud-and-dragon designs.

sentences.zh: 九嬪冠服：嘉靖十年始定，冠用九翟，次皇妃之鳳。

translations.literal: Crowns and dress of the Nine Concubines: first fixed in Jiajing 10; the crown used nine pheasants, ranking below the imperial consort's phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: The crowns and dress of the Nine Concubines were first fixed in Jiajing 10 (1531): the crown bore nine pheasants, ranking below the imperial consort's phoenix.

sentences.zh: 大衫、鞠衣，如皇妃制。

translations.literal: Great robe and ju robe, as under the imperial consort regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The great robe and ju robe followed the imperial consort's regulations.

sentences.zh: 圭用次玉谷文。

translations.literal: The tablet used secondary-grade jade with grain pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The jade tablet was of secondary grade, carved with a grain pattern.

sentences.zh: 內命婦冠服，洪武五年定，三品以上花釵、翟衣，四品、五品山鬆特髻，大衫為禮服。

translations.literal: Crowns and dress of inner-court titled ladies, fixed in Hongwu 5: third rank and above wore flower hairpins and pheasant robes; fourth and fifth ranks wore the pine-mountain special topknot; the great robe served as ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: The crowns and dress of inner-court titled ladies were fixed in Hongwu 5 (1372): those of third rank and above wore flower hairpins and pheasant robes; fourth and fifth ranks wore the pine-mountain special topknot; the great robe served as ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 貴人視三品，以皇妃燕居冠及大衫、霞帔為禮服，以珠翠慶雲冠，鞠衣、褙子、緣襈襖裙為常服。

translations.literal: Noble ladies were treated as third rank: for ceremonial dress they used the imperial consort's private-residence crown with great robe and cloud collar; for everyday dress, the Pearl-and-Kingfisher Auspicious-Cloud Crown with ju robe, over-jacket, and bordered jacket and skirt.
translations.idiomatic: Noble ladies were accorded third-rank status: for ceremonial dress they wore the imperial consort's private-residence crown with great robe and cloud collar; for everyday dress, the Pearl-and-Kingfisher Auspicious-Cloud Crown with ju robe, over-jacket, and bordered jacket and skirt.

sentences.zh: 宮人冠服，制與宋同。

translations.literal: Palace attendants' crowns and dress: regulations the same as under the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants' crowns and dress followed Song-dynasty regulations.

sentences.zh: 紫色，團領，窄袖，遍刺折枝小葵花，以金圈之，珠絡縫金帶紅裙。

translations.literal: Purple, round collar, narrow sleeves, embroidered throughout with broken-branch small sunflowers circled in gold, pearl net, gold-sewn belt, red skirt.
translations.idiomatic: They wore purple round-collared jackets with narrow sleeves, embroidered throughout with broken-branch sunflowers circled in gold, a pearl net, a gold-sewn belt, and a red skirt.

sentences.zh: 弓樣鞋，上刺小金花。

translations.literal: Bow-shaped shoes, embroidered above with small gold flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Bow-shaped shoes were embroidered with small gold flowers.

sentences.zh: 烏紗帽，飾以花，帽額綴團珠。

translations.literal: Black gauze cap, ornamented with flowers; the cap front set with round pearls.
translations.idiomatic: A black gauze cap ornamented with flowers had round pearls set on the brow.

sentences.zh: 結珠鬢梳。

translations.literal: Knotted-pearl temple tress combs.
translations.idiomatic: Knotted-pearl temple tress combs completed the headdress.

sentences.zh: 垂珠耳飾。

translations.literal: Hanging-pearl ear ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Hanging-pearl ear ornaments completed the set.

sentences.zh: 皇太子冠服：陪祀天地、社稷、宗廟及大朝會、受冊、納妃則服袞冕。

translations.literal: The crown prince's crown and dress: when assisting at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, and the ancestral temple, and at great court assemblies, receiving investiture, and taking a consort, he wore the ceremonial crown and robe.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's crown and dress: when assisting at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, and the ancestral temple, and at great court assemblies, investiture, and betrothal, he wore the full ceremonial crown and robe.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年定，袞冕九章，冕九旒，旒九玉，金簪導，紅組纓，兩玉瑱。

translations.literal: Fixed in Hongwu 26: ceremonial robe with nine emblems, crown with nine pendants, nine jade pieces on the pendants, gold hairpin guide, red cord chin strap, two jade ear-plugs.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed in Hongwu 26 (1393): a nine-emblem ceremonial robe, a crown with nine pendants bearing nine jade pieces, a gold hairpin guide, a red cord chin strap, and two jade ear-plugs.

sentences.zh: 圭長九寸五分。

translations.literal: The tablet was nine inches five tenths long.
translations.idiomatic: The jade tablet measured nine and a half inches.

sentences.zh: 玄衣纁裳，衣五章，織山、龍、華蟲、宗彝、火；

translations.literal: Dark upper garment and deep-red skirt; the robe bore five emblems, woven with mountain, dragon, flowering creature, ritual vessels, and fire;
translations.idiomatic: The dark upper garment and deep-red skirt bore five emblems on the robe—mountain, dragon, flowering creature, ritual vessels, and fire—woven in place;

sentences.zh: 裳四章，織藻、粉米、黼、黻。

translations.literal: the skirt four emblems, woven with waterweed, millet grain, axe-and-gouge, and opposed triangles.
translations.idiomatic: the skirt four emblems—waterweed, millet grain, axe-and-gouge, and opposed triangles.

sentences.zh: 白紗中單，黻領。

translations.literal: White gauze inner robe, opposed-triangle collar.
translations.idiomatic: The inner robe was white gauze with an opposed-triangle collar.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝隨裳色，織火、山二章。

translations.literal: The knee cover followed the skirt's color, with fire and mountain emblems woven in two grades.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover matched the skirt in color and bore fire and mountain emblems in two grades.

sentences.zh: 革帶，金鉤苾，玉佩。

translations.literal: Leather belt, gold hook and Bi ornament, jade pendants.
translations.idiomatic: There was a leather belt with gold hook and Bi ornament, and jade pendants.

translations.literal: Five-colored sash
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial sash used five colors

sentences.zh: 織成，純赤質，三百三十首。

translations.literal: woven complete, of pure red substance, three hundred thirty tassels.
translations.idiomatic: fully woven, of pure red thread, with three hundred thirty tassels.

sentences.zh: 小綬三，色同。

translations.literal: Three small sashes, colors the same.
translations.idiomatic: Three smaller sashes matched the colors.

sentences.zh: 間織三玉環。

translations.literal: Three jade rings woven between them.
translations.idiomatic: Three jade rings were spaced along them.

sentences.zh: 大帶，白表朱裡，上緣以紅，下緣以綠。

translations.literal: Great belt, white outside and vermilion inside, red edging above and green edging below.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt was white without and vermilion within, with red edging above and green below.

sentences.zh: 白襪，赤舄。

translations.literal: White stockings, red court shoes.
translations.idiomatic: White stockings and red court shoes completed the dress.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年定，冕冠，玄表朱裡，前圓後方，前後各九旒。

translations.literal: Fixed in Yongle 3: ceremonial crown, dark outside and vermilion inside, round in front and square behind, nine pendants before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3 (1405) the ceremonial crown was fixed: dark without and vermilion within, round in front and square behind, with nine pendants before and behind.

sentences.zh: 每旒五采繅九就，貫五采玉九，赤、白、青、黃、黑相次。

translations.literal: Each pendant had five-colored silk with nine tassels, strung with nine five-colored jade pieces—red, white, green, yellow, and black in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Each pendant used five-colored silk with nine tassels, strung with nine five-colored jade pieces—red, white, green, yellow, and black in sequence.

sentences.zh: 玉衡金簪，玄紞垂青纊充耳，

translations.literal: Jade crossbar and gold hairpin, dark cord hanging green silk ear-plugs to fill the ears,
translations.idiomatic: A jade crossbar and gold hairpin secured the crown; a dark cord hung green silk ear-plugs to fill the ears,

translations.literal: supported by a white-jade ear-plug, vermilion strap and chin tassel.
translations.idiomatic: supported by a white-jade ear-plug on a vermilion strap and chin tassel.

sentences.zh: 玉圭長九寸五分，以錦約其下，並韜。

translations.literal: The jade tablet was nine cun five fen in length; brocade bound its lower end, and a separate pouch sheathed it.
translations.idiomatic: The jade tablet was nine cun and five fen long; brocade bound its lower end, and a pouch sheathed it entirely.

sentences.zh: 袞服九章，玄衣五章，龍在肩，山在背，火、華蟲、宗彝在袖，

translations.literal: The sacrificial robe had nine emblems; the dark upper garment five emblems: dragon on the shoulders, mountain on the back, fire, flowering creature, and ritual vessels on the sleeves,
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial robe bore nine emblems: the dark upper garment had five—dragon on the shoulders, mountain on the back, and fire, flowering creature, and ritual vessels on the sleeves,
